overview.en: The analysis of the dataset reveals that the best performing model is K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), which achieved the highest accuracy. metrics_overview.en: This table compares how well different machine learning models predict the target variable, HPR. A practical caution is that while KNN performs well, the model's performance relies heavily on the quality and relevance of all input features, so continuous data validation is necessary.

fig6ab_mse_r2_features.en: This chart, titled 'MSE and R² vs feature count,' helps us understand how adding more data features affects the accuracy of our predictions. The R² score measures how well our model explains the variation in the data, with higher values being better (closer to 1). The Mean Squared Error (MSE) measures the average squared difference between predicted and actual values, with lower values being better (closer to 0). Overall, the KNN model performed best, achieving an R² of 0.817 and an MSE of 0.0128, particularly when using 9 features (VFA, Butyrate, Acetate, VSS, Propionate, Ethanol, COD-O, pH, and ORP_Low). This suggests that while adding features is generally helpful, there is an optimal balance, and adding too many features might not improve performance or could even hurt it. A practical caution is that the best performance is achieved with a specific, limited set of features, rather than simply using all available data points.
